stem: A child with acute abdominal pain is lying very still with the hips flexed; what condition is this posture most suggestive of?
explanation: Peritonitis is the best answer. A child with peritonitis may lie very still and keep the hips flexed because movement worsens abdominal pain.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Approach to Acute Abdominal Pain

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because constipation does not typically cause the characteristic still, hips-flexed posture described here.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because psychosocial stress may contribute to symptoms, but it does not explain this peritonitic guarding posture.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because peritonitis commonly causes a child to lie motionless with the hips flexed to reduce pain from peritoneal irritation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because polyuria is a urinary symptom and is not associated with this abdominal posture.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because diet-related discomfort does not produce the classic still, hips-flexed posture of peritonitis.
